Takeaways
Revenue
-- Net sales from continued operations grew 30% to $1.8 billion in the quarter, attributed to the metal packaging EMEA acquisition, pricing actions, and favorable FX, offset by a nearly 2% decline in volume and mix.
Adjusted EBITDA
-- Fourth quarter adjusted EBITDA increased 10% to $272 million, with a 51 basis point margin expansion driven by operational discipline despite softer volumes.
Adjusted EPS
-- Adjusted EPS was $1.05, representing a 5% increase, with gains due to favorable price/cost in the consumer segment, productivity improvements, FX benefits, and lower SG&A, partially offset by volume softness, higher interest, and lost earnings from divestitures.
Debt reduction
-- Net debt was reduced approximately 40% year over year through $966 million repayment in the quarter and $2.7 billion reduction for the full year, aided by $656 million ThermoSafe divestiture proceeds and free cash flow.
Net leverage ratio
-- The net leverage ratio dropped from 6.4x at the start of the year to approximately 3x at year-end, surpassing the targeted 2026 range of 3.3x-3x ahead of schedule.
ThermoSafe divestiture
-- ThermoSafe, the temperature-assured packaging business, was sold in early November for $656 million, a transaction valued at roughly 13x earnings.
Full year performance
-- Full year net sales for continued operations advanced 42% to $7.5 billion, with adjusted EBITDA up 28% to $1.3 billion and margin expanding 120 basis points to 16.9%.
Full year adjusted EPS
-- Adjusted EPS for the year was $5.71, up 17%, driven by acquisitions, favorable pricing, productivity, and FX, but offset by divestitures, volume headwinds, higher taxes, and interest expense.
Operating cash flow
-- Operating cash flow reached $690 million, including $216 million in one-time items ($196 million taxes on capital gains from divestiture); normalized full year operating cash flow was $906 million.
2026 guidance
-- 2026 revenue is projected between $7.25 billion and $7.75 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $1.25 billion to $1.35 billion, adjusted EPS of $5.80 to $6.20, and operating cash flow of $700 million to $800 million, with about $100 million in taxes from 2025 divestitures included.
Pro forma growth targets
-- Compared to 2025 pro forma sales of $7.3 billion and EPS of $4.97, 2026 is expected to see low- to mid-single-digit sales growth and approximately 20% EPS growth, with the latter partly offset by a 150-200 basis points hike in effective tax rate.
Segment operational highlights
-- U.S. Metal Packaging achieved record quarterly and annual performance, with food can units up 10% in Q4 and 9% for the full year; EMEA food can units fell 3%, with customers managing lower than historical inventory levels.
Portfolio transformation
-- The strategic portfolio transformation and simplification, including consolidation of metal and rigid paper containers under one structure, is now complete and expected to deliver further synergies and margin enhancement.
Margin expansion plan
-- Management targets cumulative 200 basis points of EBITDA margin improvement and $150 million to $200 million in cost savings by 2028, primarily through structural simplification and coordinated productivity initiatives.
Capital allocation
-- More than 80% of 2025 cash flow and divestiture proceeds went to debt reduction; capital spending is expected to normalize at approximately 4% of sales, focused on automation, AI, and targeted technology upgrades.
